description: The line plot illustrates the similarity of hidden state activations (HSAs) between English and four other languages—English (en&en), Spanish (en&es), Greek (en&el), and Bengali (en&bn)—across all 24 layers of the Qwen1.5-1.8B model. The horizontal axis, labeled “Layer,” spans from 0 to 24 in integer increments, representing the depth of the transformer architecture. The vertical axis, labeled “Similarity,” ranges from 0.00 to 0.45 in steps of 0.05, quantifying the degree of alignment between HSAs of paired languages. The red line (en&en) begins at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, rises to a peak of 0.26 at layer 6, then gradually declines to 0.08 by layer 20 before surging to 0.43 at layer 23. The blue line (en&es) starts at 0.06, peaks at 0.24 at layer 6, and remains relatively flat around 0.06 from layer 20 onward, showing no late-stage increase. The green line (en&el) and pink line (en&bn) follow similar trajectories: both begin near 0.04 and 0.03 respectively, peak at 0.15 and 0.13 at layer 6, dip to 0.05 by layer 20, and then climb sharply to approximately 0.30 at layer 23. Notably, between layers 6 and 20, the en&es similarity (blue) consistently exceeds that of en&en (red), which is counterintuitive given that identical-language comparisons typically exhibit higher similarity.
caption_used: The similarity of HSAs in different languages across all layers within Qwen1.5-1.8B is depicted. The line plot shows four language pairs: 'en&en' (red), 'en&es' (blue), 'en&el' (green), and 'en&bn' (pink). The horizontal axis represents the layers, ranging from 0 to 24, while the vertical axis indicates similarity, ranging from 0.00 to 0.45. The red line starts at approximately 0.07 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.26, and then declines steadily to 0.08 at layer 20 before sharply increasing to 0.43 at layer 23. The blue line begins at 0.06 at layer 0, peaks at layer 6 with a value of 0.24, and then stabilizes around 0.06 from layer 20 onward, showing no significant increase. The green and pink lines exhibit similar trends, starting at 0.04 and 0.03 respectively, peaking at layer 6 with values of 0.15 and 0.13, and then declining to 0.05 at layer 20 before increasing to 0.3 at layer 23. Notably, the similarity between 'en&es' consistently exceeds that of 'en&en' across layers 6 to 20, contrary to expectations.
